newsitem.title: PERU: Peru extends emergency rule in capital Lima.
newsitem.headline: Peru extends emergency rule in capital Lima.

text.p: The Peruvian government extended Tuesday for 60 days state-of-emergency rule in 19 districts of the capital Lima, the adjoining port of Callao, and three provinces in the jungle departments of Huanuco and Ucayali.

A decree in the official daily El Peruano said the extensions were needed "because disturbances to internal order still exist and it is necessary to complete the process of pacification in these areas of the country."
Emergency rule, decreed to give the government a free hand in combatting leftist guerrillas, places areas under the control of armed forces and suspends many constitutional rights.
Despite a dramatic overall drop in rebel attacks since the height of the conflict between the mid-1980s and the early 1990s, emergency rule continues in about 30 percent of Peruvian territory.
Wars unleashed by the Maoist Shining Path guerrillas and the smaller Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) have claimed 30,000 lives since 1980.
